title: Letter and Harbor
premise: In the winter of 1919, Emrys Thackeray keeps a private ledger of soldiers' names that official reports omit, believing history happens elsewhere. When a mute child is abandoned at her harbor-side clinic with a note reading 'forget the face,' Emrys discovers the boy witnessed a massacre his commanding officer's report has erased. Pursued by officers determined to bury the truth and aided by a disgraced war correspondent, a smuggler widow, and the child himself, she races to get testimony on record before a tribunal seals the victors' version forever. The book ends with Emrys testifying at cost to her own freedom, the ledger entered into evidence, and the child — given a name at last — finding a found family in the harbor town.
about_author: Kestrel Thackeray is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unclaimed letters from wartime field hospitals. They write from a coastal cottage, where they claim the tide brings in better stories than any archive.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Names
chapters.summary: Emrys Thackeray, a battlefield nurse turned harbor-clinic keeper, records in her private ledger the names official reports omit. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: quiet defiance and loneliness; she believes history happens to other people, elsewhere.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: A child is left at the clinic door with a note: 'forget the face.' He does not speak, but he flinches at uniforms. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: reluctant responsibility; her first crack of curiosity about what he saw.

chapters.title: The Boy Who Would Not Speak
chapters.summary: Emrys nurses the boy, whom she calls Sparrow, and notices he draws the same burning building over and over. A visiting officer asks pointed questions about 'a stray.' POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: protective instinct hardening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Brought In
chapters.summary: Disgraced correspondent Aldous Wren arrives seeking a story no paper will print; he recognizes something in Sparrow's drawings. POV: Aldous. Emotional beat: guilt and hunger for redemption through one true story.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on the Map
chapters.summary: Sparrow's drawings match a coastal hamlet officially listed as evacuated, not destroyed. Emrys and Aldous compare notes against her ledger. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: dread as omissions become a pattern.

chapters.title: Captain Hale's Courtesy
chapters.summary: Captain Hale visits the clinic with gifts and veiled threats, offering Emrys funding if she surrenders the child. She refuses. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: fear met with stubbornness; loyalty vs. truth begins its tug.

chapters.title: Sparrow Speaks
chapters.summary: Terrified by a nightmare, Sparrow finally speaks: soldiers burned his village after the armistice, and an officer ordered witnesses silenced. POV: Sparrow (close third). Emotional beat: shattering release; trust given for the first time.

chapters.title: The Widow Merrow
chapters.summary: Smuggler widow Bess Merrow offers her boat and her network to move Sparrow to safety, asking nothing — yet. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: gruff warmth; the found family begins assembling.

chapters.title: Ledger Against Report
chapters.summary: Emrys and Aldous reconstruct the timeline: her ledger of dead and missing contradicts the official account name by name. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: grim purpose; the ledger becomes ammunition.

chapters.title: The Search Party
chapters.summary: Hale's men search the harbor district. Bess hides Sparrow among cargo; Emrys lies to a soldier's face for the first time. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guilt and exhilaration; justice outside the law begins.

chapters.title: A Witness in the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: They find a surviving fisherman from the village hiding in the old lighthouse, willing to testify if his family is protected. POV: Aldous. Emotional beat: fragile hope that hardens into resolve.

chapters.title: The Tribunal Announced
chapters.summary: News breaks of a military tribunal that will close the inquiry within three weeks — victors' historians already drafting the record. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: the clock starts; time is running out.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Someone informs on them; the lighthouse witness vanishes. Suspicion falls on everyone, even gently on Sparrow's silence. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: paranoia fracturing the found family's trust.

chapters.title: Hale's Offer, Again
chapters.summary: Hale corners Emrys alone, revealing he knows about her ledger and offering amnesty in exchange for it and the boy. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: temptation of safety weighed against the dead's right to be named.

chapters.title: The Missing Page
chapters.summary: Emrys discovers a page torn from her ledger — and realizes the informant is the clinic's kind young assistant, coerced by threats to his own family. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: heartbreak and unexpected mercy.

chapters.title: Storm Passage
chapters.summary: Bess runs the boat through a storm to reach a second survivor and recover the vanished fisherman, held in a coastal depot. POV: Bess. Emotional beat: courage against nature and empire alike.

chapters.title: What We Owe the Dead
chapters.summary: Around a smuggler's fire, each character reckons with why the truth matters: Aldous for his printed lies, Bess for her lost sons, Emrys for every unnamed patient. POV: rotating close thirds. Emotional beat: the found family binds itself by vow.

chapters.title: The Depot Raid
chapters.summary: Aldous and Bess extract the fisherman while Emrys creates a diversion using her nurse's authority. It nearly costs Sparrow, left briefly unprotected. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: terror and triumph braided together.

chapters.title: Sealed Doors
chapters.summary: The tribunal refuses civilian testimony; Hale moves to have Sparrow committed as a ward of the state. Legal avenues close one by one. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: despair before the last gambit.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Names
chapters.summary: Outside the tribunal, Emrys publicly reads her ledger aloud, name by name, as crowds gather and Aldous wires the story abroad. The tribunal cannot ignore the spectacle. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: climax; grief transfigured into testimony.

chapters.title: Cross-Examination
chapters.summary: Forced to convene hearings, the tribunal calls Emrys; Hale's cross-examination turns on her lawbreaking. Sparrow takes the stand and identifies Hale's superior. POV: Emrys and Sparrow. Emotional beat: the cost paid; truth enters the record.

chapters.title: Letter and Harbor
chapters.summary: Months later: the report is amended, Hale court-martialed, Emrys lightly sentenced and pardoned. She gives Sparrow a real name and a home; the found family gathers at the harbor. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: resolution — history kept, belonging earned.
